calendar2027.event: Spring Festival (Chinese New Year) Official Public Holiday
calendar2027.dates: 2027-02-05 to 2027-02-13 (9 consecutive days; CNY Day 1 is Sat Feb 6, 2027)
calendar2027.impact: Ends 2 days before the Feb 15 trip window opens. Make-up workdays fall on Sun Jan 31 and Sun Feb 14, 2027. Return-travel Chunyun rail/flight congestion and select independent restaurant Lunar New Year closures can extend into Feb 15–20.
calendar2027.sourceName: Beijing Municipal Government (State Council 2027 Holiday Schedule, published Nov 2026)

calendar2027.impact: Traditional end of Spring Festival celebrations; major lantern displays (e.g., Yuyuan Garden in Shanghai) draw peak evening crowds and require timed entry or ticket confirmation.

calendar2027.dates: Historically opens Mar 4–5 (exact 2027 closing date not yet officially decreed as of Nov 25, 2026)
calendar2027.impact: Heightened security, periodic Tiananmen Square / Forbidden City / central Beijing road and metro access restrictions, and elevated hotel rates in Beijing CBD & Dongcheng during early March. Favor late February (Feb 21–28) or mid-March (Mar 15–22) for Beijing, or visit Shanghai first.
calendar2027.sourceName: State Council of the People's Republic of China
calendar2027.flaggedNote: Exact 2027 NPC/CPPCC opening/closing dates are typically formalized in Dec 2026 / Jan 2027.

calendar2027.impact: Falls after the Mar 23, 2027 trip window; zero overlap.
calendar2027.sourceName: Beijing Municipal Government (State Council 2027 Holiday Schedule)

calendar2027.impact: Eligible citizens of 57 countries (including US, Canada, UK, and most EU nations) may stay up to 240 hours (10 days) across 24 provinces/municipalities (including inter-provincial travel between Shanghai and Beijing) via 65 open ports ONLY with a confirmed onward ticket to a third country/region (e.g., US → China → Hong Kong/Tokyo/Seoul → US). Standard round-trip itineraries (US ↔ China) or stays >10 days require a Chinese tourist (L) visa unless passport qualifies for unilateral 30-day visa-free entry.

climateNormals.travelTakeaway: Cool and damp in late Feb; noticeably milder (10°C avg) with higher rain (~97mm) in March. Pack waterproof layers and umbrella.
Very dry (~6–10mm precip, ~2 rainy days/month) but sub-freezing nights in Feb; March warms quickly to 13.6°C highs with crisp clear Great Wall views.

michelinClusters.edition: MICHELIN Guide Shanghai, Jiangsu & Zhejiang 2026 (released Apr 9, 2026)
michelinClusters.notes: No. 1 Mainland China Michelin cluster by both total starred (51) and total city listings (156 at ceremony; live guide.michelin.com index reflects 153 due to mid-year closures/updates). Dense subway-connected core across Huangpu (The Bund, Xintiandi), Jing'an, Changning, Xuhui, and Lujiazui (Pudong). Active edition throughout Feb–Mar 2027 (next edition historically April).
michelinClusters.sourceName: MICHELIN Guide Official Ceremony Release (Apr 9, 2026) & Shanghai Municipal Government

michelinClusters.notes: No. 2 Mainland China Michelin starred cluster (33 starred, including 2 Three-Star restaurants — most in Mainland China) with freshly published 2027 ratings active for Feb–Mar 2027. Concentrated in Chaoyang (CBD / Guomao / Sanlitun) and Dongcheng (Wangfujing / Hutongs), linked seamlessly by Beijing Subway Lines 1, 2, 5, 6, 8, and 10.
Strongest Bib Gourmand concentration in Mainland China (52 Bib Gourmand; 117 total). Milder Feb–Mar subtropical climate; pairs well with Shenzhen (59 total) or Hong Kong/Macau via High-Speed Rail.
Sichuan dining powerhouse with freshly published 2027 edition including 1 Three-Star restaurant.

michelinClusters.edition: MICHELIN Guide Shanghai, Jiangsu & Zhejiang 2026 (released Apr 9, 2026)
michelinClusters.notes: Zhejiang province totals 142 listings (Hangzhou accounts for 88 listings, including 2 Two-Star, 11 One-Star, and 1 MICHELIN Green Star at Pu Zhu).
